nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the value of a finite word $d_0 d_1 \cdots d_{m-1}$ of digits $d_i \in \{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}$ is the natural number $\sum_{i < m} d_i k^i$, so the first digit is the least significant one; the empty word has value $0$.
nodes.title: Value of a base-$k$ digit word, least significant digit first

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number and let $a$ be a sequence indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. If $b$ belongs to the $q$-kernel of $a$ and $j < q$, then the sequence $n \mapsto b(qn + j)$ also belongs to the $q$-kernel of $a$.
nodes.title: The $q$-kernel is closed under decimation

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $r$ be positive natural numbers and let $a$ be a sequence indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. If the $p^r$-kernel of $a$ is finite, then the $p$-kernel of $a$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the $p$-kernel from the $p^r$-kernel

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $p$ and $r$ and every sequence $a$ indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, the $p^r$-kernel of $a$ is contained in the $p$-kernel of $a$.
nodes.title: The $p^r$-kernel lies in the $p$-kernel

nodes.summary: For every natural number $q$, every sequence $a$ indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ belongs to its own $q$-kernel.
nodes.title: A sequence lies in its own kernel

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and let $B$ be a finite alphabet. A sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to B$ is $k$-automatic if and only if it is a coding of a prolongable $k$-uniform fixed point.
nodes.title: Cobham's characterization of automatic sequences

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $B$ a finite alphabet. If a sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to B$ is $k$-automatic, then there are a natural number $q$, an infinite word $u$ over the alphabet $A = \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}$ and a map $g : A \to B$ such that $w$ is morphic with generator $u$ and coding $g$.
nodes.title: Automatic sequences are morphic

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $B$ a finite alphabet. If a sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to B$ is a coding of a prolongable $k$-uniform fixed point, then there are a natural number $q$, an infinite word $u$ over the alphabet $A = \{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}$ and a map $g : A \to B$ such that $w$ is morphic with generator $u$ and coding $g$.
nodes.title: Uniform fixed-point codings are morphic

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and let $B$ be a finite alphabet. nodes.title: Uniform fixed-point codings via iterates of a uniform map

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $B$ a finite alphabet. A sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to B$ is a coding of a prolongable $k$-uniform fixed point when $k \ge 2$ and there are a nonempty finite alphabet $A$, a map $f$ sending each letter of $A$ to a word of length exactly $k$ over $A$, a letter $a \in A$ with $f(a) = a\alpha$ for some nonempty word $\alpha$ over $A$, a sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to A$ and a map…
nodes.title: Codings of prolongable uniform fixed points

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $a$ be a sequence indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ with values in a finite type $B$. Then $k \ge 2$ and the $k$-kernel of $a$ is finite (that is, $a$ is $k$-automatic in the finite-kernel sense) if and only if $k \ge 2$ and some deterministic finite automaton with output, reading base-$k$ digits least significant first, outputs $a(n)$ on every word of base-$k$ digits whose value is $n$,…
nodes.title: Eilenberg's theorem: finite kernel iff automatic

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $B$ a finite alphabet. A sequence $w : \mathbb{N} \to B$ is $k$-automatic when $k \ge 2$ and there is a deterministic finite automaton with output, consisting of a nonempty finite set of states $Q$, an initial state $s \in Q$, a transition map $\delta : Q \times \{0, 1, \dots, k-1\} \to Q$ and an output map $\tau : Q \to B$, such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every finite…
nodes.title: Automatic sequences via finite automata

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a sequence $a$ indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ is $k$-automatic when $k \ge 2$ and the $k$-kernel of $a$ is finite.
nodes.title: $k$-automatic sequence (finite-kernel definition)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a sequence $a$ indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, the $k$-kernel of $a$ is the set of all sequences $n \mapsto a(k^e n + r)$ with $e, r \in \mathbb{N}$ and $r < k^e$.
nodes.title: The $k$-kernel of a sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
